title: Row vs Columnar and Parquet Internals: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Row vs Columnar and Parquet Internals: Visual Guide

1. Bytes You Pay For | a slider over how many of 50 columns a query touches, with row and columnar cell grids and the GB actually read | storage charges for contiguous bytes, so the columnar saving is proportional to the fraction of columns touched and disappears when a query wants whole records

2. Inside A Parquet File | the file layout from PAR1 to footer, with the five-step read path from tail fetch to page decode | the footer at the end describes every column chunk's byte range, so a reader issues range GETs for only the chunks it needs

3. The Row Group Dial | row group size dragged from 1 MB to a whole 2 GB file, showing splits, footer entries and writer memory | small groups waste requests and defeat compression while large ones collapse parallelism and blow up memory, and the right value follows what your storage charges for

4. Proving Absence | four predicate shapes run against six row groups' min, max and null counts, marking skipped, useful and wasted reads | statistics prove absence and never presence, so surviving groups are still filtered row by row, and != prunes only when min equals max

5. Sorted Or Shuffled | the same 24 row groups written sorted by timestamp and in arrival order, with a one-hour predicate window overlaid | statistics are only as good as your clustering, so identical data and identical machinery skip 96% of the file or none of it
